title: OSHA Crane Operator Certification Checklist (29 CFR 1926.1427)
subtitle: Use before an operator is assigned to a crane and during site inspections of crane work.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
If an item is a Defect, stop the operator from running the equipment until it is corrected, and record what was done.
The crane manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks beyond this list.

sections.title: Certification and licensing
items: A certificate or license for the operator covers the equipment being operated
Where the jurisdiction runs a qualifying crane operator licensing program, the operator holds that license
License is within the period set by the licensing office and no more than 5 years old
Certificate from an accredited testing organization was issued within the last 5 years
Certificate states the equipment type the operator is certified for
An audited employer program certificate was issued by the operator's current employer
Operator confirms the employer provided the certification or license without charging them
Certification documentation notes the language the test was given in
Operations manual and load charts on the equipment are in the language of the certification

sections.title: Operator evaluation
items: Signed evaluation document for the operator can be produced at the worksite
Record shows operator's name, evaluator's name and signature, date, and make, model and configuration of equipment used
Crane in use was used in the evaluation, or the employer can show it needs no substantially different skills or knowledge
Blind lifts, personnel hoisting or multi-crane lifts planned for the operator were part of the demonstrated hoisting activities
Evaluator named on the record has the knowledge, training and experience to assess crane operators
Any operator retrained under (b)(5) has a re-evaluation on the retraining subject

sections.title: Operator-in-training supervision
items: A trainer is on site watching the operator-in-training the whole time the equipment is operated
Trainer works for the trainee's employer or acts as its agent
Trainer is doing no other tasks while monitoring
Trainer and trainee can see each other directly and communicate by voice or hand signals
Trainer and trainee are in direct communication
Breaks last 15 minutes or less, with no more than one per hour
Trainer told the trainee the specific tasks and limits immediately before the break

sections.title: Restricted work for operators-in-training
items: Trainee is not operating where equipment, load line or load could reach within 20 feet of a line up to 350 kV or 50 feet of a line over 350 kV
Trainee is not operating equipment used to hoist personnel
Trainee is not operating in a multiple-equipment lift
Trainee is not operating over a shaft or cofferdam or in a tank farm
Trainee does multiple-lift rigging only where the trainer has determined their skills are sufficient

references: 29 CFR 1926.1427: Operator training, certification, and evaluation (Subpart CC: Cranes and Derricks in Construction)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, current as of 2026-11-09
